diagnostic_evidence.quote: Specifically, our experiments suggest that for any sufficiently large $k$ and $\kappa$, we can find a problem instance for which the backward error of \algne\ after $k$ iterations is at least $\min\{1, \log_{10}(\kappa)/k\}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The introduction states as fact that a family of hard instances is constructed for which the MINBERR-NE backward error after k iterations is at least log(kappa(A))/k. The paper contains no theorem or proof of any lower bound for MINBERR-NE; the only support is the hedged empirical statement in the experiments section ('our experiments suggest ... at least min{1, log10(kappa)/k}'). The claimed lower-bound construction is therefore unsupported as stated.

failure_location.quote: However, we are able to construct a family of hard problem instances for which the \algne\ backward error is at least $\log(\kappa(\A))/k$ after $k$ iterations

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Rephrase the introduction sentence as an empirical observation (matching the experiments section), or state and prove the corresponding lower bound.
issues.overall_effect: Readers are told a hard-instance lower bound is constructed/proven for MINBERR-NE when only numerical evidence is given.
issues.title: Introduction asserts a constructed log(kappa)/k lower bound for MINBERR-NE that the paper only supports empirically
issues.why_classification: A local rewording (or an added proof) resolves it; no formal result or guarantee changes.

issues.failure_explanation: In eq:GRQ/eq:MM the parametrization is z=[-1;y], so [b,AQ_k]z = AQ_k y - b. The eigenvector of the pencil for the smallest finite eigenvalue sigma_min(T_k)^2 is W[0;v_min]=[alpha;v_min]; scaling it to satisfy the constraint z_1=-1 gives y=-v_min/alpha, so the minimizer of backward error over K_k is x_k = -(1/alpha)Q_k v_min. The proof instead normalizes the eigenvector to first entry +1 ('parallel to [1;y]', and it asserts that (1/alpha_hat)W[0;v_hat] has first element -1 when it is +1), yielding y=+v_min/alpha, which minimizes ||AQ_k y + b||/||y|| rather than ||AQ_k y - b||/||y||. Since backward error is not even in x, the formula's output can have much larger error than the minimizer: e.g. A=diag(2,1), b=(1,1), k=1 gives alpha=-3/(2*sqrt(2)); the formula returns -(2/3)(1,1) with backward error sqrt(29)/4 ~ 1.35, whereas the true MINBERR solution (2/3)(1,1) has backward error 1/4. Consequently Algorithm alg:MINBERR (final step), Algorithm alg:MINBERRnonsym (final step) and Proposition prop:minberrNE output the negation of the intended solution, and the guarantees of thm:minberrcost and c:minberr fail for the algorithms as written.

failure_location.quote: the smallest eigenpair of the generalized eigenvalue problem~\eqref{eq:MM} is given by $(\sigma_{\min}^2,\frac1\alpha\v_{\min})$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Flip the sign: define alpha=(1/||b||_2)((T_k)_{1,1}(v_min)_1+(T_k)_{1,2}(v_min)_2) (resp. alpha=(1/||b||_2)(B_k)_{1,1}(v_min)_1), or write x_k=-(1/alpha)Q_k v_min, in Lemma l:quotient, Proposition prop:minberrNE and the final steps of both algorithms.
issues.overall_effect: Both algorithms return the negation of the backward-error minimizer, so the computed solution generally has large (not epsilon) backward error; the output contracts of alg:MINBERR and alg:MINBERRnonsym and the approximation guarantees in thm:minberrcost and c:minberr are unfulfilled as written.
issues.title: Sign error in the MINBERR solution formula: the recovered vector is the negation of the backward-error minimizer
issues.why_classification: A one-line, local sign correction (in four places) restores every stated claim and guarantee; no lemma, rate, regime, or complexity bound is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The smallest eigenvalue $\lambda_{\min}$, which is nonnegative, is equal to the square of the backward error of the MINBERR solution, that is, $\lambda_{\min} =  (\berr_{\A,\b}(\x_k))^2$.
If we write $\x=\Q_k\y$, then minimizing $\berr_{\A,\b}(\x)=\frac{\|\A\x-\b\|_2}{\|\A\|_2\|\x\|_2}$ over $\x\in\Kc_k(\A,\b)$ reduces to minimizing the following generalized Rayleigh quotient:
if this breaks down (i.e., $\sigma_{\min}(\tilde\T)=\berr_{\A,\b}(\x_k)<\epsilon$), proceed to step 7.

issues.failure_explanation: Since ||Q_k y||_2 = ||y||_2, min_{x in K_k} berr(x) = (1/||A||_2) min_y ||AQ_k y - b||_2/||y||_2 = sigma_min(T_k)/||A||_2, and the smallest pencil eigenvalue equals ||A||_2^2 * berr(x_k)^2 (the setup in eq:GRQ itself shows the constant 1/||A||_2 is dropped when passing to the Rayleigh quotient). The identities lambda_min = berr^2, berr(x_k)=sigma_min(T_k) and berr(x_hat)=||T_k v_hat||_2/||v_hat||_2 hold only when ||A||_2 = 1, which is never assumed. Counterexample: A=diag(2,1), b=(1,1), k=1: sigma_min(T_1)=1/2 and lambda_min=1/4, but min berr = 1/4, so berr^2=1/16 != lambda_min. Consequently the stopping tests in alg:MINBERR (Cholesky of G-eps^2 I, i.e. sigma_min(T)<eps) and alg:MINBERRnonsym (dqds with shift eps^2) actually test berr < eps/||A||_2: for ||A||_2 < 1 the algorithms can terminate with backward error exceeding eps (output contract violated), and for ||A||_2 > 1 they iterate up to k ~ sqrt(3||A||_2/eps), so c:minberr's O((1/sqrt(eps))(T_A+n+log(1/delta))) complexity fails for matrices of large norm.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the factor ||A||_2 (berr = sigma_min(T_k)/||A||_2, lambda_min = ||A||_2^2 berr^2) in Lemma l:quotient and Proposition prop:minberrNE, and compare sigma_min(T_k) (resp. sigma_min(B_k)) with eps*||A||_2 in the stopping tests (using a standard constant-factor norm estimate if ||A||_2 is not known).
issues.overall_effect: The stated eigenvalue/backward-error identities, both algorithms' convergence tests and output contracts, and the complexity (and, for ||A||_2<1, the correctness) of Corollary c:minberr are unreliable for any A with ||A||_2 != 1; thm:minberrcost's proof also relies on the defective identity.
issues.title: Missing 1/||A||_2 factor: backward error equals sigma_min(T_k)/||A||_2, not sigma_min(T_k), miscalibrating both algorithms' stopping tests
issues.why_classification: A local constant-factor correction (plus a standard, routine norm estimate) restores all identities, guarantees, and the advertised complexity; no mathematical content is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: When $\A$ is PSD, the same holds unless $\A\b=0$, that is, $\b$ lies in the null space of $\A$.

issues.failure_explanation: From the definition of alpha one gets alpha=0 iff b^T A Q_k v_min = 0, i.e. b orthogonal to the single direction A Q_k v_min; b orthogonal to all of A Q_k is sufficient but not necessary, so 'precisely when' is false. Moreover, for PSD A, alpha=0 can occur with Ab != 0: for A=diag(1,0), b=(1,1), k=2 the Lanczos coefficients are alpha_1=alpha_2=1/2, beta_2=1/2, beta_3=0, so T_2=[[1/2,1/2],[0,0]], v_min=(1,-1)/sqrt(2) and alpha=0 while Ab=(1,0)!=0 and b^T A Q_2 != 0. (In this regime the argmin in the lemma need not exist, the infimum being approached only as ||x|| grows without bound.)

failure_location.quote: Unless $\alpha=0$; which happens precisely when $\b$ is orthogonal to the entire subspace $\A\Q_k$, as we see by examining~\eqref{eq:GRQ}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the footnote: alpha=0 iff b^T A Q_k v_min = 0; for PSD A this can occur once K_k contains a null vector of A (with Ab != 0), in which case the infimum of the backward error equals sigma_min(T_k)/||A||_2 but need not be attained.
issues.overall_effect: The stated conditions under which the lemma's recovery formula is valid are incorrect; a reader could apply it believing alpha=0 is ruled out whenever Ab != 0.
issues.title: Footnote mischaracterizes the alpha = 0 degenerate case of Lemma l:quotient
issues.why_classification: A footnote-level correction; no theorem, algorithm, or guarantee depends on the erroneous characterization.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In particular, for a $1/2$-relative error ($\Delta = 0.5$), we require $\ell \geq 2.23 \ln(n/\delta^2)$.

issues.failure_explanation: For Delta=1/2, Lemma lemma:invit requires ell >= 0.5 + ln(64k ln(2/delta)/(pi delta^2))/(2 ln 1.25) = 7.25 + 2.2407*ln(k/delta^2) + 2.2407*ln ln(2/delta), where 1/(2 ln 1.25) = 2.2407 > 2.23. This strictly exceeds 2.23 ln(k/delta^2) for every k>=2 and delta in (0,1) (e.g. k=1000, delta=0.01: required ~47 vs claimed ~36), so the 'In particular' specialization and the proof of thm:minberrcost apply the lemma below its hypothesis, and the loop counts 'While ell < 2.23 ln(k/delta^2)' in alg:MINBERR and alg:MINBERRnonsym run too few inverse-iteration steps for the (1+1/2)-relative accuracy with probability 1-delta to be established.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 2.23 ln(k/delta^2) in the theorem and both algorithms by a bound satisfying the lemma, e.g. ell >= 2.25(ln(k/delta^2)+ln ln(2/delta))+8, which is still O(ln(k/delta^2)) so all complexity claims are unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The probability-1-delta approximation guarantee of Theorem thm:minberrcost (and hence of Corollary c:minberr) is unproven for the algorithms as specified.
issues.title: Inverse-iteration count 2.23 ln(k/delta^2) is below Lemma lemma:invit's own sufficient bound
issues.why_classification: A constant/lower-order-term adjustment of the loop count restores the guarantee; the asymptotic complexity and the form of the theorem are preserved.

issues.failure_explanation: Standard chi-square upper tails (Laurent-Massart: P(chi^2_m >= m+2 sqrt(mx)+2x) <= e^{-x}) give sum c_j^2 <= n + 2 sqrt(n ln(2/delta)) + 2 ln(2/delta) with probability 1-delta/2, which is not <= n ln(2/delta) when ln(2/delta) <~ 1. Indeed, for delta close to 1 (e.g. delta=0.9, ln(2/delta) ~ 0.80) and large n with |S_high| ~ n, P(sum c_j^2 > n ln(2/delta)) -> 1, so the claimed 1-delta/2 probability bound is false in that regime and the lemma's stated iteration count is unproven there.

failure_location.quote: $\sum c_j^2$ follows $\chi^2_{|S_{\mathrm{high}}|}$, so by~\cite[Eqn.~(4.3)]{laurent2000adaptive} we see that with probability $1-\delta/2$, we have $\sum c_j^2 \leq n \ln(2/\delta)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Carry the correct tail bound (e.g. sum c_j^2 <= n+2 sqrt(n ln(2/delta))+2 ln(2/delta), or 2n ln(2/delta) for delta below a fixed constant) through the computation; only constants inside the logarithm change, so the lemma's form and all downstream complexities survive.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma lemma:invit is unsupported as written for large delta, and in that regime the guarantees built on it (thm:minberrcost, c:minberr) are also unproven.
issues.title: Chi-square tail bound misapplied in the proof of Lemma lemma:invit
issues.why_classification: A constant-bookkeeping correction in the proof; the lemma's conclusion and all its uses (with adjusted constants) survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We note that inverse iteration would then break down in exact arithmetic, but in finite precision converges with excellent accuracy~\cite{peters1979inverse}, often in one step.
Once $k=\tilde n$, $\Q_k$ contains a null vector of $\A$,

issues.failure_explanation: The corollary is stated for PSD (possibly singular) A, but its proof combines t:minberr with thm:minberrcost, which hypothesizes A ≻ 0. For singular A, once the Krylov space contains a null vector of A, the matrix T_k is singular and the inverse-iteration solves with T^T and T are undefined in exact arithmetic; the paper acknowledges the breakdown but supports it only by finite-precision heuristics and an unformalized regularization alternative, so the probability-1-delta guarantee and the stated complexity are not established for the singular matrices the corollary covers. (In this regime the argmin defining the MINBERR iterate may also fail to exist, the infimum being approached only in the limit.)
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either restrict c:minberr to A ≻ 0, or formalize the already-sketched workaround: run MINBERR on A+tau*||A||_2*I with tau and the internal tolerance chosen below epsilon and convert via Lemma l:composition, which preserves the stated complexity up to constant factors.
issues.overall_effect: c:minberr's guarantee and complexity are unproven on part of its stated scope (singular PSD inputs).
issues.title: Corollary c:minberr claims A ⪰ 0 but the supporting theorem assumes A ≻ 0; the algorithm breaks down for singular A in exact arithmetic
issues.why_classification: The source itself supplies the bypass (regularization plus Lemma l:composition); formalizing it is a contained, routine argument preserving the claim and complexity.

issues.failure_explanation: By Theorem t:minberr, k iterations guarantee backward error at most 3/(k^2-1), and 3/(k^2-1) <= eps requires k >= sqrt(3/eps+1). For k = ceil(sqrt(2/eps)) we only have k^2 >= 2/eps, so the guaranteed bound is 3/(k^2-1) <= 3/(2/eps-1) = 3eps/(2-eps) > eps for every eps in (0,1) (e.g. eps=0.02: k=10, bound 3/99 ~ 0.030 > 0.02). Even the conjectured sharp constant 2 would require k^2 >= 2/eps+1. Hence the stated count does not guarantee eps backward error.

failure_location.quote: If we fix the number of iterations upfront (e.g., to be $\lceil\sqrt{2/\epsilon}\rceil$, which guarantees that backward error is bounded by $\epsilon$), then we can bypass steps 4--5.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace ceil(sqrt(2/eps)) by ceil(sqrt(3/eps+1)) (or by ceil(sqrt((2+eps)/eps)) if one assumes the conjectured constant 2).
issues.overall_effect: An implementation variant is claimed to guarantee eps backward error with an iteration count that the paper's own theorem does not support.
issues.title: Claimed fixed iteration count ceil(sqrt(2/eps)) does not guarantee eps backward error
issues.why_classification: A local constant change in a remark; no result or guarantee depends on it.

issues.failure_explanation: When alpha=0 (i.e. (B_k)_{1,1}(v_min)_1 = 0), ||A Q_k v_min||_2 = sigma_min(B_k), so along x = t*Q_k v_min the backward error tends to sigma_min(B_k)/||A||_2 as t grows; this is the infimum of the backward error over Span(Q_k) (approached but not attained), and it equals 1 only in the special case sigma_min(B_k) = ||A||_2. The footnote's value '1' is therefore false in general, although the qualitative points (non-existence of the minimizer, divergent residual norm) are correct.
